newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar interim president to run for post.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar interim president to run for post.

text.p: Madagascar's interim president Norbert Ratsirahonana has announced he will be a candidate in the November 3 presidential elections, state radio reported.
"My objective is to get Madagascar back on the rails and on the road to serious development," Ratsirahonana was quoted by the radio as saying on Friday.
The announcement sets up an election contest between Ratsirahonana and impeached former president Albert Zafy.

Ratsirahonana, prime minister and named interim president in advance of November elections, said he was running for the sake of the nation and to consolidate a structural adjustment programme with International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
Ratsirahonana, 58, a politician and lawyer, is not a member of any party, a fact that could count in his favour with the electorate, according to political analysts on the island.
Candidates must declare before midnight (2100 GMT) on Friday and campaigning starts October 13, according to electoral laws.
Former president Zafy, whose impeachment by parliament was confirmed by the Constitutional Court on September 4, has also said he would stand in the election.

The impeachment capped three years of political instability in Madagascar, the world's fourth largest island and which has a population of 14 million. Last month Ratsirahonana named a new cabinet ousting two key ministers closely associated with Zafy.
